title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has issued a response to the Committee’s 2020 report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, outlining its stance on regulating AI and ensuring safety, transparency, and accountability. It emphasises commitments to develop clear public standards, support responsible research, and engage stakeholders to align AI technology with societal values.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual explains how it will monitor and set rules for using artificial intelligence in qualifications, aiming to keep exams fair, transparent, and secure. The guidance was released after a joint request from the Secretary of State for Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business and Trade, highlighting the government’s interest in overseeing AI’s impact on the education system.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how copyrighted works are used in training AI systems, evaluating the legal and ethical implications for creators, developers, and the broader industry. It offers recommendations to balance the advancement of AI technology with the protection of intellectual property rights.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK Government responded to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report on AI, highlighting the need for urgent, coordinated action to ensure the technology is safe, fair and beneficial for society. It outlined plans to boost research, strengthen regulation, support workforce skills, and manage risks associated with rapid AI development.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document outlines the terms of reference for a committee that will review how artificial intelligence impacts public standards, detailing its scope, goals, and process. It also includes a FAQ section that explains the committee’s role, responsibilities, and expected outcomes.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on AI governance. Their submission highlights concerns and offers guidance on regulating AI systems.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy explores how AI technologies will shape the oversight and approval processes for medical products, ensuring safety and efficacy while embracing innovation. It calls for applying the AI White Paper principles to guide regulators in evaluating AI-driven medical devices and treatments.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy sets out a goal for the organization to become the most effective, efficient, trusted and influential defense entity in AI for its size. It aims to lead in AI capability, building confidence and influence both within and beyond the defense sector.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan outlines how the Department for Transport will collaborate with the transport sector to tap into AI’s benefits and improve services. It also sets out measures to identify and manage the risks that come with adopting new AI technologies.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: Progress Report: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence outlines how copyright works are used in AI development, detailing compliance with Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It reviews current practices, challenges, and recommendations to balance copyright protection with AI innovation.
